title: The Person I Was at Twenty

collection.credit: NEW EVENTS — INNER LIFE, PART V (81-100, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)

ledger.why: the casting line (the roles carry it)

collection.description: A villager watching a loud, certain young adult argue on the beach sees their own younger self.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is watching (friend), a young adult, argue passionately with a group of friends about the best way to catch octopus. (friend) is loud, certain, very funny and completely wrong. (subject) can't stop watching. It's like looking at (subject.him/her)self, twenty years ago, on that exact patch of sand.

a__fx.name: Answer A
a__fx.text: (subject) wanders over and joins in, and soon finds (subject.him/her)self arguing just as loudly as (subject.he/she) did at twenty, and just as certainly, and possibly just as wrongly. (friend) is delighted to have such a worthy opponent. Nobody wins. On the way home (subject) realizes (subject.he/she) hasn't enjoyed being wrong this much in years.

b__fx.name: Answer B
b__fx.text: (subject) stays where (subject.he/she) is. (subject.He/She) thinks about everything that person at twenty didn't know yet: the good things, the hard things, the people who hadn't arrived in (subject.his/her) life. (subject.He/She) wouldn't warn (subject.him/her) about any of it, (subject.he/she) decides. (subject.He/She) would just say: keep arguing about octopus. It was a good use of an afternoon. (subject.He/She) smiles and goes home.
